studies.Study: Teng C et al. (2023) [PMID: 36411185] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Fatty foods and the risk of bladder cancer: A case-control study.
studies.Title: Fatty foods and the risk of bladder cancer: A case-control study.
studies.Authors: Teng C, Zheng S, Wan W, Liu L, Yu S, Cao M, Lu W, Shan Y
studies.Timing: retrospective dietary assessment (food intake within 1 y)
studies.Population: Patients newly diagnosed with bladder cancer and recruited controls

sample_size.excerpt: Patients newly diagnosed with bladder cancer (n = 113) and 292 controls were recruited.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 113 + 292 = 405

cases.excerpt: Patients newly diagnosed with bladder cancer (n = 113) and 292 controls were recruited.

effect_size.excerpt: There was clear and positive association between soybean oil and bladder cancer risk with OR of 3.47 (95 % CI, 1.69-7.14).

confidence_interval.excerpt: There was clear and positive association between soybean oil and bladder cancer risk with OR of 3.47 (95 % CI, 1.69-7.14).

comparison.excerpt: High soybean oil intake was a risk factor for bladder cancer.

design.excerpt: Fatty foods and the risk of bladder cancer: A case-control study.

timing.excerpt: A food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was used to investigate the food intake within 1 y.

continent.excerpt: much higher than the Chinese recommended dietary intake

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The consumption of soybean oil, the largest proportion of cooking oil, in both groups were much higher than the Chinese recommended dietary intake

gender.excerpt: In stratified analyses by sex and smoking status, the relationship was similar for most results

smoking_status.excerpt: In stratified analyses by sex and smoking status, the relationship was similar for most results
